judgments.reasoning_cat1: The execution date is garbled/blank ("July ¥, 2005"), yet it fixes the defined "Effective Date".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That defect propagates to §1.9 Employment Term, §1.14 Restricted Period and §8.1 ("third anniversary of the Effective Date"), and the preamble also makes both Ajuba entities the joint "Company" while §2.2 puts all payment duties only on Ajuba India.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition with a single plain meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mild friction with §2.1, which has him report to the Board "(or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)", and with Schedule 2.1's "Reports to the Chairman", but the definition itself is clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list closed by the catch-all "and other related services" and the open-ended "such other entities serviced by the Company", a textbook general-vs-specific / ejusdem generis problem in the term that drives the non-compete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach is contested against §1.6 "Core Business" and Article V(a)/(d), and against the separate Non-Competition Agreement preserved by §9.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition with no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Code" is never used anywhere else in the instrument, an orphan definition but not a contradiction of any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "known to the Employee as a consequence of or through the Employee's employment" is vague and the punctuation leaves it unclear which items the qualifier attaches to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds §4.1 (assignment only "upon the Company's request") and §4.2 (property of the Company already), which do not sit perfectly together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all information, in whatever form, regarding Parent, the Company their Business" is missing a comma and the "including, without limitation" list leaves the outer boundary of the definition undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §3.1's carve-outs and Exhibit A ¶2's separate "Company Information and Property" definition; the two overlap but do not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The (a)/(b)(i)/(b)(ii) structure with a nested "more than the sum of (A) and (B)" test is grammatically tangled, and limb (a) is so broad it swallows the whole Business, making "Core Business" arguably no narrower.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That matters directly because Article V(d) substitutes "Core Business" for "Business" on an §8.4 termination; if (a) is co-extensive with §1.2 the substitution is meaningless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "actively sought" and "material contact" are vague boundary terms in a restrictive covenant definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It measures periods from "the date of termination of this Agreement" while Article VIII terminates *employment*, and §1.14 measures the Restricted Period from the end of the Employment Term — inconsistent reference points.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is technical but self-contained; the lower-case "any fiscal year" against the defined "Fiscal Year" is a small slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Making Ajuba's own regularly employed accountants the arbiter sits alongside §2.2(b)'s EBITDA bonus table and §2.2(a)'s salary trigger without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the third anniversary of this Agreement" is a slightly different measuring point from the defined Effective Date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §8.1 says "third anniversary of the Effective Date" and §1.14 keys the Restricted Period to "the end of the Employment Term", so early termination under Article VIII creates a real question whether the Term ends then or in 2008.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain calendar definition with a standard change mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the fiscal-year bonus tables in §2.2(b) and the audited-statements timing there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming definition with one meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in §1.5, §1.7, Article V(b) and §9.9's third-party-beneficiary carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but plainly worded catch-all definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Person" appears only in §2.1(b) and nothing else turns on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Geographically definite, though "territories and protectorates" is an archaic term of uncertain modern content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with §1.2's "United States and India" limitation on the Business.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-year post-term restraint is definite in words but the endpoint depends entirely on when "the end of the Employment Term" falls.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with §1.9 (term ends on the third anniversary "unless earlier terminated") the period could run three or six years, and §9.8 preserves a separate Non-Competition Agreement that may set a different period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "duties as are customarily performed by a President", "full professional and business-related time" and "such other legally permissible and proper duties" are all vague, and the clause both incorporates and pre-emptively amends Schedule 2.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says he reports to the Board while Schedule 2.1 says he "[r]eports to the Chairman of the Board", it makes Schedule 2.1 override the Bylaws, and it deems Schedule 2.1 amended by the §8.4(a) consolidations that Schedule 2.1 assigns to him.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The $300,000 trigger — "retroactive to the first business day of the year following the Fiscal Year in which such EBITDA was achieved" — is confusing as to which year the increase starts and whether it can occur more than once.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with §2.2(b)'s identical $3.5m EBITDA threshold and with §8.4's "compensation at the rate or level, as applicable, in effect on the date of such termination".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "eligible to receive" against a fixed table is soft, and the FY2007 sentence ("unless such employee is terminated pursuant to Sections 8.3 or 8.4 after December 31, 2007") is awkwardly conditioned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 each say the Company has no liability for "any other bonus" for the prior or current year while §§8.3 and 8.4 then expressly preserve the prior-year Bonus — an internal pull the court would have to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An entitlement immediately qualified by "may be modified or discontinued at the sole discretion of the Company" — the promise and the discretion sit uneasily but the words are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §8.4(c) makes a breach of §2.2 Good Reason, so unfettered discretion to discontinue benefits arguably empties that trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "substantially similar to the D&O Policy maintained ... immediately prior" is a benchmark standard but reasonably determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with §2.2(c) benefits and §8.4(c); no competing provision addresses D&O cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Samii" is never identified, "net sales" is undefined, and the quoted phrase "goes live" has no definition, all in a payment formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Critically, §§8.3 and 8.4 pay the Reorganization Bonus "in accordance with Section 2.2(e)" — which is this commissions clause, not the Reorganization Bonus in 2.2(f).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "when and if" shut down/restructured, and "after the Reorganization Bonus was earned", leave the earning moment uncertain, and the subclause is mislabelled "(f".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.3 and 8.4 both cross-refer the Reorganization Bonus to "Section 2.2(e)", which is Commissions — a mis-citation that has to be construed, and Schedule I defines completion by lease terminations that Ajuba, not Employee, controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable out-of-pocket expenses" is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §8.4(c) makes breach of §2.3 Good Reason, but nothing contradicts the reimbursement obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard confidentiality covenant with four conventional and well-drafted exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §1.5, §3.3 and Exhibit A ¶13; consistent, although Article VII mis-cites the confidentiality article as "Article I".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear return-and-delete obligation triggered by termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps Exhibit A ¶2's broader "Company Information and Property" return duty, which is cumulative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "legitimate business purposes" is an undefined and elastic exception that essentially self-defines the Company's freedom to disclose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical phrase reappears in Exhibit A ¶13, and the asymmetry against Employee's absolute duty in §3.1 is a one-sided-drafting point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment is conditioned on "the Company's request" and covers technology "acquired during the Employment Term", which is broad but readable; the heading is numbered "4." not "4.1".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §4.2 already declares all Company Technology "is and shall remain the property of the Company", which is hard to square with a present assignment that only happens on request.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain return-and-destroy obligation; the missing "all" before "electronically stored copies" is trivial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against §4.1's request-triggered assignment, so ownership is asserted before any assignment is made.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "engage in any activity which is in competition with the Business", "directly or indirectly" and the open list ending "or otherwise" make the restraint's outer edge genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope depends on §1.2 Business, is swapped for §1.6 Core Business by V(d) on an §8.4 termination, runs for the §1.14 Restricted Period, and coexists with the separate Non-Competition Agreement preserved by §9.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "canvas, solicit or accept" extends to passive acceptance, and "induce any Customer to patronize any business directly or indirectly in competition" is broad but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the §1.7 Customer definition, whose measuring date ("termination of this Agreement") does not match Article VIII's termination of employment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is genuinely unclear whether the "having the title of Supervisor and above" qualifier attaches only to Indian employees or also to "any employee in the United States", and the carve-out sentence then only mentions India.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The proviso's reference to "the preceding sentence" is ambiguous given the sentence contains two distinct prohibitions; no other provision resolves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short substitution rule whose effect depends entirely on two other definitions; on its own face it is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is triggered only by an §8.4 termination, so characterising the termination (Company without cause / Good Reason / employee resignation under §8.5) decides which covenant applies — a classic relational dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgment of reasonableness; it states a conclusion rather than an operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Article VII's blue-pencil sentence, which contemplates the very overbreadth this clause disclaims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional three-limb representation with a written-disclosure carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §9.8 acknowledges a separate Non-Competition Agreement of even date, so limb (iii) is arguably inaccurate unless that agreement counts as disclosed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict representation, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with §6.1 and §9.8; nothing else in the instrument cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It twice cites "Articles I, IV or V" when Article I is the definitions article and the confidentiality covenants are in Article III, and it refers to "the Company's rights under Article VII hereof" inside Article VII itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-references do not match Articles III and VIII as they exist, and the blue-pencil sentence also has to be reconciled with §9.2 severability and Article V(e)'s reasonableness acknowledgment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the earliest of ... or the first to occur" is redundant but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the third anniversary "of the Effective Date" while §1.9 says the third anniversary "of this Agreement", a small mismatch given the garbled preamble date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "conduct causing ... substantial public disgrace or disrepute" and "gross misdemeanor" are vague, limb (d) opens with a stray "or", and limb (c) cites "Articles I, IV, V or VI" when Article I is definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanket fifteen-day cure right cannot sensibly apply to the completed acts in (a), and the article citation does not match Article III's confidentiality covenants that Article VII treats as the protected ones.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Disability definition (120 days in any 240-day period, "as determined by competent medical evidence") is workable; the payout sentence is dense but readable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pays the Reorganization Bonus "in accordance with Section 2.2(e)", but 2.2(e) is Commissions and the Reorganization Bonus is 2.2(f) — a cross-reference that contradicts the compensation article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "material diminution", the tangled proviso about consolidation/elimination/outsourcing, and "the compensation at the rate or level, as applicable" (salary only? bonus too?) are all genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mis-cites the Reorganization Bonus to "Section 2.2(e)", overlaps §8.5 (which also lets the Employee resign for any reason, with no severance), and its carve-out collides with Schedule 2.1's grant of cash management and finance responsibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An employee resignation whose effective date is "chosen by the Company" is an odd, internally strained mechanic, and "thirty (30) business days" is unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §8.4 expressly gives the Employee "the right to terminate his employment ... for Good Reason or for any other reason pursuant to this Section 8.4", which overlaps this section and carries very different pay consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings clause with one meaning; the section number is OCR'd as "OI".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the instrument turns on headings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional severability language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VII instead directs the court to modify and enforce overbroad restraints, and Exhibit A ¶18 uses a reformation formula — three differently worded approaches to the same problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence limits "any waiver" to the terms of "such written waiver" although the first sentence never requires waivers to be in writing — a drafting slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause protects only the Company's rights, an asymmetry against §8.4's Employee rights, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "assigned by the Company only (a) ... (b)" is a closed list, yet the final sentence binds and benefits "assigns" generally — an expressio unius tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "the Company" is defined as both Ajuba and Ajuba India, so a merger or asset sale of only one entity leaves the assignment mechanics uncertain, which matters for who may enforce Article V.
